# `sandloom.sdk.errors`

Exceptions a module may raise or catch.

Public API 1.0 (spec §2.2, Appendix C).

`from sandloom.sdk.errors import <name>`. Signatures in a terminal: `sandloom docs <name>`. Beginner names are the ones generated code and the examples use; any other name is advanced (mark its import line `# sandloom: advanced <reason>` in generated code and examples).

## Advanced names

### `AuditUnavailableError`

```python
class AuditUnavailableError(RuntimeError)
```

A `required` audit write could not be performed.

Raised by `record_audit` (`required` is the default since 0.7) when
there is no UoW scope, the backend has no audit store, or the actor id is
not a UUID — a security/compliance action must fail loudly rather than
silently skip its audit trail.

### `BlockUnavailableError`

```python
class BlockUnavailableError(RuntimeError)
```

The emergency-block mark could not be written / removed (cache outage).

### `ConsumerDefinitionError`

```python
class ConsumerDefinitionError(DeclarationError)(
    message: str,
    *,
    fix: str | None = None,
) -> None
```

An invalid `@on` consumer (SANDLOOM-B016).

### `ContractArgumentError`

```python
class ContractArgumentError(ContractCallError, TypeError)(
    detail: Any = None,
    *,
    status_code: int | None = None,
    headers: Mapping[str, str] | None = None,
    code: str | None = None,
) -> None
```

The call's arguments do not bind to / validate against the signature (422).

Raised BEFORE the provider runs, locally and remotely alike: unknown or
missing arguments, positional-only / keyword-only violations, or a value
that does not validate against the parameter's annotation.

### `ContractCallError`

```python
class ContractCallError(HTTPException)(
    detail: Any = None,
    *,
    status_code: int | None = None,
    headers: Mapping[str, str] | None = None,
    code: str | None = None,
) -> None
```

A contract call failed with a declared status — identical locally and over RPC.

Every domain / protocol error a contract raises surfaces to the caller as
this exception (an `HTTPException`): a provider `HTTPException` or an
`http_status`-protocol exception is converted with the SAME status,
JSON-encoded `detail`, `headers` (e.g. `Retry-After`) and `code`
whether the provider is in-process or behind internal RPC. Framework errors
keep their own subclass on both paths (`ContractIdempotencyConflict`,
`ContractArgumentError`, …).

### `ContractIdempotencyUnavailable`

```python
class ContractIdempotencyUnavailable(ContractCallError, RuntimeError)(
    detail: Any = None,
    *,
    status_code: int | None = None,
    headers: Mapping[str, str] | None = None,
    code: str | None = None,
) -> None
```

The command dedupe store is unreachable: the command is refused (503).

Commands fail CLOSED — running one without dedupe could duplicate its side
effect on a caller retry.

```python
    headers: Mapping[str, str] | None = None,
    code: str | None = None,
) -> None
```

A retried command already completed but its result was too large to keep (409).

The effect happened exactly once; only the result body is unavailable.

### `ModuleRegistrationConflict`

```python
class ModuleRegistrationConflict(RuntimeError)
```

A buffered registration would conflict with live kernel state.

Raised by `ModuleRegistrationDraft.preflight` BEFORE anything is
applied, so a conflicting module leaves the kernel completely untouched.

### `ReadContractWriteError`

```python
class ReadContractWriteError(RuntimeError)
```

A read contract tried to write (its UoW is always rolled back).

Raised for published events, queued `on_commit` / `before_commit`
effects, `record_audit` rows and ORM / DML writes — which a rolled-back
read would otherwise drop silently while returning success. Declare the
method `@contract_method(command=True, idempotency_key=...)`.

### `RemoteServiceUnavailable`

```python
class RemoteServiceUnavailable(HTTPException)(
    service_name: str,
    *,
    reason: str,
    code: str = 'remote_service_unavailable',
) -> None
```

A remote service binding exists, but the provider cannot serve the call.

Transport / trust failures only (unreachable, timeout, a request or
response that does not authenticate, provider crash) — never a domain
error, which
reaches the caller as the provider's own status. For `reason="timeout"`
the remote call MAY HAVE COMMITTED: retrying a decorated command with the
same idempotency argument replays its result instead of re-executing it.
`code` names the failure for programmatic handling.

### `RoutePolicyError`

```python
class RoutePolicyError(DeclarationError)(

    *,
    fix: str | None = None,
) -> None
```

A route is both `public()` and authenticated (SANDLOOM-B008).

### `SagaDefinitionError`

```python
class SagaDefinitionError(ValueError)
```

A saga definition is malformed or does not match its contracts.

Raised when the definition is built (structure) and at startup (the called
contracts); the message names the saga, the step and a `fix:`.

### `ServiceNotFound`

```python
class ServiceNotFound(ServiceRegistryError)
```

Base error for service registry.

### `ServiceUnavailableInDeployment`

```python
class ServiceUnavailableInDeployment(HTTPException, ServiceNotFound)(
    service_name: str,
    *,
    reason: str | None = None,
) -> None
```

A contract is neither provided locally nor bound to a remote provider.

Raised by `CoreFacade.get_service` so the configurable monolith degrades
*explicitly* (501 Not Implemented) instead of a bare 500 when, in this
deployment topology, nobody implements the contract. Subclasses
`ServiceNotFound` so existing `except ServiceNotFound` handlers and the
RPC server's not-found mapping keep working unchanged.

Lives here (next to `ServiceNotFound`) rather than in `sandloom.core.rpc` so
the facade can raise it WITHOUT importing the concrete RPC mechanism; the
RPC package re-exports it as part of its public API.

### `TaskEnqueueConflict`

```python
class TaskEnqueueConflict(HTTPException)() -> None
```

An HTTP exception you can raise in your own code to show errors to the client.

This is for client errors, invalid authentication, invalid data, etc. Not for server
errors in your code.

Read more about it in the
[FastAPI docs for Handling Errors](https://fastapi.tiangolo.com/tutorial/handling-errors/).

## Example

``python
from fastapi import FastAPI, HTTPException

app = FastAPI()

items = {"foo": "The Foo Wrestlers"}

@app.get("/items/{item_id}")
async def read_item(item_id: str):
    if item_id not in items:
        raise HTTPException(status_code=404, detail="Item not found")
    return {"item": items[item_id]}
``

### `TenantMismatchError`

```python
class TenantMismatchError(RuntimeError)
```

A tenant-owned object does not belong to the bound tenant.

### `UnitOfWorkRequiredError`

```python
class UnitOfWorkRequiredError(RuntimeError)
```

A guaranteed write-path effect was requested outside a Unit of Work.

Raised by `publish_event` when no UoW scope is active and the caller
did not opt into best-effort semantics (`record_audit` raises its own
`AuditUnavailableError` in the same situation). Without a UoW
there is no transaction for the outbox row to commit with, so the
guarantee ("published iff the change commits, never lost") cannot hold.

### `UnsafeTenantOperationError`

```python
class UnsafeTenantOperationError(RuntimeError)
```

An ORM operation could bypass or mutate tenant ownership.
